headline: IBM and Red Hat pledge $5 billion and 20,000 engineers to patch the open-source bugs Anthropic's AI unearths at machine speed, as attackers turn stolen Fortinet credentials and freshly confirmed Cisco and SharePoint flaws into live intrusions.

emerging_trends.text: Anthropic's Claude now surfaces open-source bugs faster than maintainers can fix them, pushing IBM and Red Hat to throw 20,000 engineers at Project Lightwell, even as separate research shows the same models running ransomware from break-in to encryption.
emerging_trends.topic_title: IBM Bets $5 Billion on Fixing AI-Found Bugs

emerging_trends.text: Vendors and CISA confirmed a fresh wave of in-the-wild exploitation against enterprise mainstays this week, with Cisco admitting attackers hit its Unified CM call manager and Microsoft SharePoint falling to a patched deserialization flaw.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Cisco Confirms Unified CM Flaw Exploited

emerging_trends.text: Stolen credentials and trusted remote-access software keep feeding ransomware crews, as FortiBleed hands INC and Lynx the keys to hundreds of thousands of FortiGate firewalls and spoofed download sites bend ScreenConnect into an AsyncRAT dropper.
emerging_trends.topic_title: FortiBleed Feeds INC and Lynx Ransomware

topics.title: IBM Bets $5 Billion on Fixing AI-Found Bugs
topics.latest_developments: IBM and Red Hat assigned 20,000 engineers to a new service, Project Lightwell, to remediate the open-source flaws Anthropic's Claude keeps surfacing, and Anthropic made Claude Fable 5 widely available Tuesday night after the Trump administration lifted export controls on its frontier cybersecurity models.
topics.summary: Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview combed more than 23,000 open-source code paths this spring and routed 1,596 verified vulnerabilities to the projects that own them, a volume Tuskira found overwhelms volunteer maintainers; IBM and Red Hat now pitch Project Lightwell to close the resulting patch gap.

sources.title: Anthropic's AI Finds Bugs. IBM Bets $5B It Can Fix Them.
What the AI patch gap means for enterprise security
Trump Administration Lifts Restrictions on Anthropic's Claude Models After Cybersecurity Alarm
US lifts export controls on Anthropic's frontier cybersecurity AI models

topics.title: FortiBleed Feeds INC and Lynx Ransomware
topics.latest_developments: Researchers attributed the FortiBleed campaign—credentials harvested from hundreds of thousands of FortiGate firewalls—to the INC and Lynx ransomware operations after finding an operator tied to FortiBleed infrastructure working negotiation panels for both groups.
topics.summary: FortiBleed threw roughly 75,000 Fortinet firewalls wide open and verified the stolen credentials, which now seed follow-on network intrusions and ransomware deployment; Fortinet customers should rotate credentials and audit access.

sources.title: FortiBleed Campaign Linked to INC, Lynx Ransomware Attacks
FortiBleed Credential Theft Linked to INC and Lynx Ransomware Operations
FortiBleed credential-theft campaign linked to Lynx ransomware
Smashing Security podcast #474: Polymarket can predict the future. So how did it miss this hack?

topics.title: SharePoint RCE Under Active Attack
topics.latest_developments: CISA added SharePoint Server flaw CVE-2026-45659 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and warned that attackers now exploit the CVSS 8.8 remote-code-execution bug Microsoft patched in May.
topics.summary: The flaw arises from deserialization of untrusted data in Microsoft SharePoint Server and lets attackers run code on unpatched instances; federal agencies and enterprises must patch under CISA's directive.

sources.title: CISA: Microsoft SharePoint RCE flaw now actively exploited
CISA Warns of Actively Exploited Microsoft SharePoint Vulnerability
SharePoint RCE CVE-2026-45659 Added to CISA KEV After Active Exploitation

topics.title: Cisco Confirms Unified CM Flaw Exploited
topics.latest_developments: Cisco confirmed July 2 that attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-20230, a server-side request forgery flaw in Unified Communications Manager it patched in early June, with the first attempts observed last week and a public proof-of-concept circulating since disclosure.
topics.summary: Cisco Unified Communications Manager, the enterprise call-control platform, carries an SSRF bug that lets attackers reach internal systems; administrators should apply the June fix at once.

sources.title: Cisco finally confirms attackers exploiting Unified CM flaw
Cisco Confirms In-the-Wild Exploitation of Unified CM Vulnerability

topics.title: SEO-Poisoned Sites Deliver AsyncRAT and Ousaban
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky detailed a massive multi-language campaign that abuses the ScreenConnect remote-access tool to deploy AsyncRAT through spoofed download sites for OBS Studio, DNS Jumper, DS4Windows, and Bandicam, while Fortinet's FortiGuard Labs tracked the Brazilian banking trojan Ousaban hitting Windows users who bank in Spain and Portugal.
topics.summary: Both campaigns lean on trusted software brands and geo-targeted phishing—Ousaban opens with a fake corrupted-PDF lure and hides its payload inside an image—to plant remote-access malware and steal banking logins; users should download software only from official vendors.

sources.title: SEO-Poisoned Software Sites Abuse ScreenConnect to Deploy AsyncRAT
Ousaban Banking Trojan Targets Iberian Bank Users with Fake PDF Lures

business_politics.title: U.S. Hiring Slows Sharply in June
business_politics.latest_developments: The Labor Department reported June payrolls grew just 57,000, well short of forecasts and a sharp slowdown after three months of overperformance.
business_politics.summary: The weak reading sent Treasury yields and the dollar lower and lifted stock futures as traders bet the Federal Reserve will cut rates; the miss came against a backdrop of elevated inflation and global turmoil.

sources.title: US economy undershoots forecasts with 57,000 jobs added in June
Stock Futures Jump After June Hiring Misses Expectations

business_politics.title: Private Credit Redemptions Mount at Blue Owl
business_politics.latest_developments: Blue Owl Capital investors asked to pull $4.7 billion from flagship funds, part of more than $22 billion in second-quarter redemption requests across 20 private credit funds the FT tracks.
business_politics.summary: The persistent investor exodus from Blue Owl's semi-liquid private credit funds signals stress in a fast-grown corner of nonbank lending, though the quarter's requests eased from the prior one.

sources.title: Blue Owl hit by $4.7bn of redemption requests as investor exodus mounts
Blue Owl Investors Ask to Withdraw $4.7 Billion From Flagship Funds

business_politics.title: Russia Unleashes Massive Strike on Kyiv
business_politics.latest_developments: The overnight death toll rose to at least 17 as Russia fired 74 missiles and nearly 500 drones at Kyiv over several hours, one of the war's largest single strikes on the capital.
business_politics.summary: The barrage of ballistic and cruise missiles and waves of drones followed President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's warning that Moscow was preparing a massive strike, battering the capital as Ukraine's own long-range drones squeeze Russian fuel supplies.

sources.title: Massive Russian Strikes Pound Ukraine's Capital, Killing at Least 17
Russia unleashes huge bombardment of Kyiv

business.title: Experts Frame Kroger-Giant Eagle Deal as Consolidation
business.latest_developments: Western Pennsylvania grocery experts said Kroger's pending purchase of Giant Eagle extends a wave of consolidation sweeping the industry.
business.summary: The acquisition merges two chains with deep regional roots—O'Hara Township-based Giant Eagle and Cincinnati's Kroger, which operated here decades ago—as analysts warn consolidation is reshaping where and how the region shops.

sources.title: Experts: Kroger-Giant Eagle deal a trend in grocery industry
A tale of 2 grocery chains: Kroger's reentry into Giant Eagle's history

business.title: Pittsburgh Breweries Pour More Nonalcoholic Beer
business.latest_developments: Brewers at last month's Beers of the Burgh festival showcased far more nonalcoholic options than in past years, a shift local makers say is accelerating.
business.summary: NEXTpittsburgh reported a surge of nonalcoholic and low-alcohol brews from Pittsburgh producers, part of a national moderation trend, with Abjuration Brewing, Old Thunder, and Brew Gentlemen among those drawing notice.

sources.title: Beer in Pittsburgh is increasingly nonalcoholic, say brewers

around_town.title: Parkway East Faces 25-Day Closure
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT laid out detour routes for the coming 25-day Parkway East shutdown to replace the Commercial Street Bridge near Frick Park.
around_town.summary: The Interstate 376 closure will reroute commuters and freight for 25 days while crews replace the Commercial Street Bridge, a project Swissvale business owners warn will choke deliveries and supplier routes across the East End.

sources.title: Navigating around the detours of the upcoming Parkway East closure

around_town.title: Mt. Nebo Road Lanes Close in Sewickley Hills
around_town.latest_developments: Crews closed the eastbound lanes of Mount Nebo Road in Sewickley Hills Borough after a routine inspection found deterioration on an overpass.
around_town.summary: The Allegheny County borough shut the eastbound side of Mount Nebo Road when a bridge inspection turned up structural deterioration, with no reopening date set.

sources.title: Part of Mt. Nebo Road closed after crews discover deterioration during inspection of overpass

around_town.title: Cooling Centers Extended Through Holiday Weekend
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh kept its cooling centers open into the Fourth of July weekend as extreme heat warnings held for a third straight day, with Thursday the week's hottest.
around_town.summary: An extreme heat warning covers much of Western Pennsylvania with heat-index values above 105 through Friday, feels-like temperatures topping 100, and storms threatening the holiday weekend across the region.

sources.title: Scorching heat wave brings 100-degree feels-like temperatures for 4th of July weekend

events.title: Pittsburgh's America 250 Fourth of July
events.latest_developments: New details set the July 4 program: the Plain White T's will perform alongside line dancing and Ferris wheel rides, ahead of what the city bills as its largest-ever fireworks show.
events.summary: On Saturday, July 4, Pittsburgh's America 250 celebration—voted the nation's best by USA Today readers—will span Downtown, the North Shore, and Mount Washington, capping the day with the biggest fireworks display in city history.

around_teams.title: Pirates' Pitching Sinks Their Worst Month
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's June report card graded teamwide pitching woes as the cause of the Pirates' worst month of the season.
around_teams.summary: Beat coverage pinned Pittsburgh's June slide on a struggling bullpen and rotation, including a down year from ace Paul Skenes, even as rookie outfielder Esmerlyn Valdez's bat offered a rare bright spot.

sources.title: Pirates June report card: Teamwide pitching woes lead to the worst month of the season

team_usa.title: USMNT Turns to Belgium Without Balogun
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN analysis judged that the United States proved it can win ugly in beating Bosnia and Herzegovina and now must face Belgium in the round of 16 without suspended top scorer Folarin Balogun.
team_usa.summary: Mauricio Pochettino's side advanced 2-0 before Balogun's red card, and writers called the gritty, multifaceted win a good sign for a U.S. team that will lean on its depth against Belgium, which rallied from 2-0 down to beat Senegal in extra time.
